module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjectures around homogeneous topological spaces

This file formalizes the notion of a weakly first countable topological space and some conjectures
around those.

*References:*
* [Ar2013] Arhangeliski, Alexandr. "Selected old open problems in general topology."
  Buletinul Academiei de Ştiinţe a Republicii Moldova. Matematica 73.2-3 (2013): 37-46.
  https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf
-/

@[expose] public section

open TopologicalSpace Topology Filter Set
open scoped Cardinal

namespace Homogeneous

/--
A topological space $X$ is called *homogeneous* if for all $x, y \in X$ there is homeomorphism
$f : X \to X$ with $f(x) = y$.
-/
class HomogeneousSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  exists_equiv : ∀ x y : X, ∃ f : X ≃ₜ X, f x = y

/-- Every discrete space is homogeneous. -/
@[category test, AMS 54]
instance DiscreteTopology.toHomogeneousSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [DiscreteTopology X] :
    HomogeneousSpace X where
  exists_equiv x y := by
    classical
    use IsHomeomorph.homeomorph (Equiv.swap x y)
      (IsHomeomorph.equiv_of_discreteTopology (Equiv.swap x y))
    rw [IsHomeomorph.homeomorph_apply, Equiv.swap_apply_left]

/-- Problem 13 in [Ar2013]:
Is it true that every infinite homogeneous compact hausdorff
space contains a non-trivial convergent sequence? -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem homogeneousSpace_exists_inj_tendsto :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), ¬ Finite X → T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      HomogeneousSpace X → ∃ s : ℕ → X, s.Injective ∧ ∃ a : X, Tendsto s atTop (nhds a) := by
  sorry

/-- Problem 14 in [Ar2013]:
Is it possible to represent an arbitrary compact hausdorff space as an image
of a homogeneous compact space under a continuous mapping? -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem homogeneousSpace_exists_surjective :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      ∃ (Y : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace Y), T2Space Y ∧ CompactSpace Y ∧ HomogeneousSpace Y ∧
        ∃ f : Y → X, Continuous f ∧ f.Surjective := by
  sorry

/-- A topological space is called ω-monolithic if
the closure of every countable subspace is metrizable. -/
class CountablyMonolithicSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  metrizable_of_closure_of_countable : ∀ ⦃s : Set X⦄, s.Countable → MetrizableSpace (closure s)

/-- Every Metrizable space is ω-monolithic. -/
@[category test, AMS 54]
instance MetrizableSpace.countablyMonolithicSpace
    (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [MetrizableSpace X] : CountablyMonolithicSpace X := by
  refine { metrizable_of_closure_of_countable := ?_ }
  intros
  infer_instance

/-- Problem 15 in [Ar2013]:
Is every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact hausdorff space first countable? -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem firstCountableTopology_of_countablyMonolithicSpace :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      HomogeneousSpace X → CountablyMonolithicSpace X → FirstCountableTopology X := by
  sorry

/-- Problem 16 in [Ar2013]:
Is the cardinality of every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact hausdorff space not greater than 𝔠? -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem countablyMonolithicSpace_card_lt :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      HomogeneousSpace X → CountablyMonolithicSpace X → #X ≤ 𝔠 := by
  sorry

/-- Problem 17 in [Ar2013]:
Is it true that every nonempty ω-monolithic compact hausdorff space contains a point with a
first countable neighborhood basis?

Note: `Nonempty X` is required since the conclusion asserts the existence of a point.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem countablyMonolithicSpace_exists_nhds_generated_countable :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      Nonempty X → CountablyMonolithicSpace X → ∃ x : X, (𝓝 x).IsCountablyGenerated := by
  sorry

end Homogeneous

findings.description:
The theorem assumes `CountablyMonolithicSpace X`: X is ω-monolithic, i.e. the closure of every countable set is metrizable. Its docstring quotes Problem 17 as being about "ω-monolithic" spaces. The cited Problem 17 is about *monolithic* compact spaces. In the PDF, the ω glyph stands before "-monolithic" in Problems 15 and 16 but not in Problem 17.

In Arhangel'skii's terminology, "monolithic" is a strictly stronger notion than "ω-monolithic". It is defined in [10], the paper the source cites for this very problem, and used the same way in the 2014 Arhangel'skii–van Mill survey: nw(cl A) ≤ |A| for every A; for compacta, w(cl A) ≤ |A|. [10] even poses the two versions side by side (Problem IV.1: "monolithic (ℵ0-monolithic)").

Every monolithic compactum is ω-monolithic. I checked this in Lean: with `IsMonolithic X := ∀ s, ∃ B : Set (Set (closure s)), IsTopologicalBasis B ∧ #B ≤ max #s ℵ₀`, a compact T2 `IsMonolithic` space is `CountablyMonolithicSpace`. So the file's right-hand side implies the literal Problem 17.

The converse fails, at least consistently. Take a Kurepa tree T. The one-point compactification of T ∪ {its ω₁-branches}, with the tree topology, is a scattered compactum in which closures of countable sets are countable, so it is ω-monolithic. But it has a dense set of size ℵ₁ and weight ≥ ℵ₂, so it is not monolithic.

So the Lean poses a stronger conjecture over a larger class of spaces. An ω-monolithic, non-monolithic compactum with no point of first countability would make the Lean answer False while leaving the source's question open. No equivalence of the two questions is known.

Caveat: the source says Problem 17 is "hidden behind" Problems 15–16. That reasoning only works for ω-monolithic spaces, so the author may have meant ω-monolithic. Even so, as written and cited, the problem says "monolithic", and the docstring misquotes it without any note.
findings.source_evidence:
Ar2013 (https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf), §6, pp. 42–43. The source defines: "A compact space X is ω-monolithic if the closure of any countable subset of X is metrizable." Then: "Problem 15 (Arhangel'skii, 1987). Is every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact space X first-countable? ... Problem 16. Is the cardinality of every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact space X not greater than 2^ω? ... It is not difficult to notice that behind the last two question is hidden the next problem which is also open now (see [10]): Problem 17. Is it true that every nonempty monolithic compact space is first-countable at some point?" The raw PDF content stream for Problem 17 has no ω glyph before "monolithic".

[10] Arhangel'skii, Russ. Math. Surveys 42:2 (1987), p. 106: "a topological space X is called monolithic if the net weight and the density coincide for every subspace Y ⊆ X. A space X is ℵ0-monolithic if the net weight of the closure of an arbitrary countable set A ⊆ X is countable." Same paper, p. 113, Problem IV.1: "Is it true that every monolithic (ℵ0-monolithic) ℵ0-celled compact space is metrizable?"

Arhangel'skii–van Mill, Topological Homogeneity (2014), §11: "each Corson compactum X is monolithic, that is, the weight of the closure of an arbitrary subset A of X does not exceed the cardinality of A."

findings.description: The module docstring says "This file formalizes the notion of a weakly first countable topological space and some conjectures around those." That sentence was copied from FormalConjectures/Paper/WeaklyFirstCountable.lean. This file defines homogeneous and ω-monolithic spaces and states Problems 13–17 of [Ar2013]; nothing here concerns weakly first countable spaces. The reference line also misspells the author as "Arhangeliski, Alexandr"; it should be A. V. Arhangel'skii.
findings.source_evidence: Ar2013, Section 6 "Homogeneous compacta" (pp. 42–43) contains Problems 13–17, about homogeneous and (ω-)monolithic compacta. The weakly first-countable problems (2–4) are in Section 3 and are formalized in a different file.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace it with e.g. "This file formalizes homogeneous and ω-monolithic topological spaces and Problems 13–17 of [Ar2013] about homogeneous compacta." Fix the author name to "Arhangel'skii, A. V.".

reformulations.difference: The source asks for a "non-trivial convergent sequence", i.e. a convergent sequence that is not eventually constant. The Lean asks for an injective sequence `s : ℕ → X` with `Tendsto s atTop (𝓝 a)` for some `a`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An injective sequence is never eventually constant. Conversely, in a T1 space take s → a, not eventually constant. Then T = range s \ {a} is infinite: otherwise Tᶜ would be an open neighbourhood of a, forcing s to be eventually equal to a. Enumerate T injectively by t. For every neighbourhood V of a, only finitely many n have s n ∉ V, so only finitely many points of range s lie outside V. Since t is injective, t n ∈ V for all but finitely many n, so t → a. Compact T2 spaces are T1, so the two readings agree.

The printed text says "monolithic". The "hidden behind Problems 15–16" remark favours ω-monolithic. The reference he gives, [1987, Russ. Math. Surveys 42:2], has no numbered problem matching Problem 17, though it discusses points of first countability in (weakly/approximately) ℵ0-monolithic spaces in §4. The finding is filed at confidence 0.55 for this reason.
review.notes:
**Other declarations**
- `HomogeneousSpace`, the two test instances, and Problems 13, 14, 15 and 16 faithfully state the source's questions.
- All use the source's blanket convention that compact means compact Hausdorff (T2 is assumed everywhere). The `answer(sorry)` polarities match the questions, and none of the hypotheses is vacuous.
- Empty and finite spaces are handled correctly.
- Problem 13 corresponds to [10] Problem 1.11 (Rudin); Problem 14 to [10] Problem III.1 ("Is every compact space the continuous image of a homogeneous compact space?").
- `CountablyMonolithicSpace` (closures of countable sets metrizable) is exactly the source's definition of ω-monolithic for compact spaces.
- Its docstring speaks of arbitrary topological spaces. For non-compact spaces this is stronger than the standard definition (nw(cl A) ≤ ω), but every use in the file is under CompactSpace + T2Space, so no statement is affected.

**Lean checks** (scratch files, `lake env lean`):
- Proved that monolithic compact T2 implies `CountablyMonolithicSpace`, and hence that the file's Problem 17 right-hand side implies the literal (monolithic) version.
- Proved the non-trivial-sequence equivalence for Problem 13.
- Confirmed that the empty space is homogeneous and that Problem 14 holds trivially for empty X.

**Status**
- All five problems are tagged research open.
- The 2014 Arhangel'skii–van Mill survey still lists Rudin's problem as unsolved. It also says it is unknown whether βω is a continuous image of a homogeneous compactum without a weight bound (Problem 14).
- arXiv API searches (math.GN, through Sept 2026) turned up no solution of Problems 13–17.
- I therefore report no status issues; the literature search was not exhaustive.

**Minor, not filed**
- The name `countablyMonolithicSpace_card_lt` says "lt" but the statement uses ≤ (naming only).
- The source's side remark that every compact LOTS is ω-monolithic looks false (the double arrow space is a separable non-metrizable compact LOTS), but it is not formalized here.

not_demonstrated.reason: Both the file's ω-monolithic statement and the source's monolithic Problem 17 are open, so neither can be proved or refuted in a few lines. The only example I know of an ω-monolithic compact space that is not monolithic needs a Kurepa tree, which exists only under extra set-theoretic assumptions, and a real topology formalization. A compiled scratch proof (scratch2.lean) shows the file's version implies the literal one, but it uses my own definition of 'monolithic' and only shows the file's statement is at least as strong, not that it is wrong.

submission.summary: No trivial demonstration is possible. The reported defect changes the class of spaces in an open problem ('monolithic' becomes 'ω-monolithic'). Both versions are open, and no small computable case tells the two notions apart. The file's statement implies the source's (checked in scratch2.lean with my own definition of 'monolithic'); the converse is not known.
submission.gave_up_reason: The only reported misformalization (Homogeneous.countablyMonolithicSpace_exists_nhds_generated_countable) uses a different class of spaces in an open problem: ω-monolithic instead of the source's 'monolithic'. Both versions are open, so neither the file's statement nor its negation has a short proof. The only example I know separating ω-monolithic from monolithic compact spaces needs a Kurepa tree, which exists only under extra set-theoretic assumptions, so it can't be done in Lean without new axioms. It would also need substantial topology. No trivial_proof.lean was created.

submission.summary: Problem 17 of [Ar2013] is about monolithic compact spaces, but the file stated it for ω-monolithic ones and misquoted the source. I added a `MonolithicSpace` class: the closure of every set A has a base of size at most max(|A|, ℵ₀). For compact Hausdorff spaces this is the same as the 1987 network-weight definition, as the docstring explains. I also added a sorry-free test showing that monolithic compact Hausdorff spaces are ω-monolithic. Problem 17 is now stated faithfully as the new theorem `Homogeneous.monolithicSpace_exists_nhds_generated_countable`, using `MonolithicSpace X`, with a corrected docstring. The reported declaration `countablyMonolithicSpace_exists_nhds_generated_countable` keeps its statement and tags. Its docstring now labels it the ω-monolithic variant of Problem 17 and explains that a positive answer would settle Problems 15, 16 and 17. As a safe, trivial extra, I fixed the module docstring's copy-pasted description and added the 1987 reference. The file compiles; the only warnings are the 6 expected `declaration uses 'sorry'`.

/-!
# Conjectures around homogeneous topological spaces

This file formalizes the notions of homogeneous, ω-monolithic and monolithic topological spaces
and some conjectures around those.

*References:*
* [Ar2013] Arhangeliski, Alexandr. "Selected old open problems in general topology."
  Buletinul Academiei de Ştiinţe a Republicii Moldova. Matematica 73.2-3 (2013): 37-46.
  https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf
* [Ar1987] Arhangel'skii, A. V. "Topological homogeneity. Topological groups and their continuous
  images." Russian Mathematical Surveys 42.2 (1987): 83-131.
  https://www.mathnet.ru/eng/rm2424
-/

@[expose] public section

open TopologicalSpace Topology Filter Set
open scoped Cardinal

namespace Homogeneous

/--
A topological space $X$ is called *homogeneous* if for all $x, y \in X$ there is homeomorphism
$f : X \to X$ with $f(x) = y$.
-/
class HomogeneousSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  exists_equiv : ∀ x y : X, ∃ f : X ≃ₜ X, f x = y

/-- Every discrete space is homogeneous. -/
@[category test, AMS 54]
instance DiscreteTopology.toHomogeneousSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [DiscreteTopology X] :
    HomogeneousSpace X where
  exists_equiv x y := by
    classical
    use IsHomeomorph.homeomorph (Equiv.swap x y)
      (IsHomeomorph.equiv_of_discreteTopology (Equiv.swap x y))
    rw [IsHomeomorph.homeomorph_apply, Equiv.swap_apply_left]

/-- Problem 13 in [Ar2013]:
Is it true that every infinite homogeneous compact hausdorff
space contains a non-trivial convergent sequence? -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem homogeneousSpace_exists_inj_tendsto :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), ¬ Finite X → T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      HomogeneousSpace X → ∃ s : ℕ → X, s.Injective ∧ ∃ a : X, Tendsto s atTop (nhds a) := by
  sorry

/-- Problem 14 in [Ar2013]:
Is it possible to represent an arbitrary compact hausdorff space as an image
of a homogeneous compact space under a continuous mapping? -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem homogeneousSpace_exists_surjective :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      ∃ (Y : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace Y), T2Space Y ∧ CompactSpace Y ∧ HomogeneousSpace Y ∧
        ∃ f : Y → X, Continuous f ∧ f.Surjective := by
  sorry

/-- A topological space is called ω-monolithic if
the closure of every countable subspace is metrizable. -/
class CountablyMonolithicSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  metrizable_of_closure_of_countable : ∀ ⦃s : Set X⦄, s.Countable → MetrizableSpace (closure s)

/-- Every Metrizable space is ω-monolithic. -/
@[category test, AMS 54]
instance MetrizableSpace.countablyMonolithicSpace
    (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [MetrizableSpace X] : CountablyMonolithicSpace X := by
  refine { metrizable_of_closure_of_countable := ?_ }
  intros
  infer_instance

/-- Problem 15 in [Ar2013]:
Is every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact hausdorff space first countable? -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem firstCountableTopology_of_countablyMonolithicSpace :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      HomogeneousSpace X → CountablyMonolithicSpace X → FirstCountableTopology X := by
  sorry

/-- Problem 16 in [Ar2013]:
Is the cardinality of every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact hausdorff space not greater than 𝔠? -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem countablyMonolithicSpace_card_lt :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      HomogeneousSpace X → CountablyMonolithicSpace X → #X ≤ 𝔠 := by
  sorry

/--
A topological space $X$ is called *monolithic* if for every $A \subseteq X$ the closure
$\overline{A}$ has a base of cardinality at most $\max(|A|, \aleph_0)$, i.e.
$w(\overline{A}) \le |A|$ (cardinal functions taking infinite values).

[Ar1987] calls $X$ monolithic if $nw(Y) = d(Y)$ for every subspace $Y$, which is equivalent to
$nw(\overline{A}) \le |A|$ for all $A$. For compact Hausdorff spaces the network weight equals the
weight, so the two definitions agree on the spaces considered below.
-/
class MonolithicSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  exists_isTopologicalBasis_closure : ∀ s : Set X, ∃ B : Set (Set (closure s)),
    IsTopologicalBasis B ∧ #B ≤ max #s ℵ₀

/-- Every monolithic compact Hausdorff space is ω-monolithic. -/
@[category test, AMS 54]
theorem MonolithicSpace.countablyMonolithicSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X]
    [CompactSpace X] [MonolithicSpace X] : CountablyMonolithicSpace X := by
  refine ⟨fun s hs => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨B, hB, hcard⟩ := MonolithicSpace.exists_isTopologicalBasis_closure s
  have hBc : B.Countable := by
    rw [← Cardinal.le_aleph0_iff_set_countable]
    exact hcard.trans (max_le hs.le_aleph0 le_rfl)
  have : SecondCountableTopology (closure s) := hB.secondCountableTopology hBc
  have : CompactSpace (closure s) := isCompact_iff_compactSpace.mp isClosed_closure.isCompact
  exact metrizableSpace_of_t3_secondCountable _

/-- Problem 17 in [Ar2013]:
Is it true that every nonempty monolithic compact hausdorff space is first countable at some
point?

Note: `Nonempty X` is required since the conclusion asserts the existence of a point.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem monolithicSpace_exists_nhds_generated_countable :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      Nonempty X → MonolithicSpace X → ∃ x : X, (𝓝 x).IsCountablyGenerated := by
  sorry

/-- Variant of Problem 17 in [Ar2013] with ω-monolithic in place of monolithic:
Is it true that every nonempty ω-monolithic compact hausdorff space is first countable at some
point?

[Ar2013] remarks that Problem 17 is "hidden behind" Problems 15 and 16. This holds for this
version: by homogeneity, a positive answer makes every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact hausdorff
space first countable, hence of cardinality at most $\mathfrak{c}$. Since every monolithic compact
hausdorff space is ω-monolithic (`MonolithicSpace.countablyMonolithicSpace`), a positive answer
also answers Problem 17.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem countablyMonolithicSpace_exists_nhds_generated_countable :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      Nonempty X → CountablyMonolithicSpace X → ∃ x : X, (𝓝 x).IsCountablyGenerated := by
  sorry

end Homogeneous
